name: outlook-calendar-list-events
description:
List upcoming events from an Outlook (Microsoft 365) calendar over a time window, through Microsoft Graph's calendarView. The output has the same shape as Google Calendar: List Events, so a workflow can swap one for the other: {count, events, window_hours, truncated, time_zone}, and per event id, uid (Graph's iCalUId, the same on every calendar the invitation sits on), summary, location, start, end, all_day, busy, show_as, event_type, response, guests, organizer_self, recurring, hangout_link, web_link and attendees [{email, response_status}]. Words are Google's: `busy` is true unless Graph's showAs is free (tentative, oof and workingElsewhere hold the time); `response` is the calendar owner's own answer (accepted, declined, tentative, needsAction, or "" for their own entry with nobody invited); `event_type` is outOfOffice for showAs oof, else default; `guests` counts the other people invited, rooms not counted; `hangout_link` is the online meeting's join URL. Times are RFC 3339 with the UTC offset of TIME_ZONE (UTC when it is not set); an all-day entry's start and end are dates, the end exclusive. A cancelled meeting still on the calendar is left out. `truncated` is true when the calendar holds more events in the window than were returned. There is no `description`: the event body is not read. Graph errors are returned as `Graph HTTP <status>: <body>` (a mailbox outside Exchange Online answers MailboxNotEnabledForRESTAPI).

Requires a vault:// reference to a Microsoft 365 OAuth access token in the AUTH_HEADER config key. The controller resolves + refreshes the token at dispatch time.

AUTH_HEADER.description: vault:// path to the OAuth access token wrapped in 'Bearer ' (e.g. 'Bearer vault://oauth/microsoft_365/{user_id}/{account_id}/access_token', where account_id is the account's Graph object id; list_connections gives the whole reference). The controller resolves + refreshes the token if expired.

CALENDAR_ID.description: Graph calendar id (from /me/calendars). Empty, or 'primary', for the account's default calendar. Letters, digits and - _ = + / only.

HOURS_AHEAD.description: Window size in hours (1–336, i.e. up to 14 days). Events overlapping now..now+HOURS_AHEAD are returned. A value outside the range is refused.

MAX_RESULTS.description: Maximum events to return (1–250; default 20). Read 50 per request, at most 6 requests. Costs roughly 180K fuel per event (measured on a recorded week of 64 events): the declared limit covers about 100, so above that set `max_fuel` on the node (250 needs about 45M). When the calendar holds more, the output's `truncated` is true. A value outside the range is refused.

TIME_ZONE.description: Optional IANA zone name (e.g. 'America/New_York'). Graph is asked for times in that zone (Prefer: outlook.timezone) and each start and end carries that zone's UTC offset on its own date, so a module can group events by local day without a time-zone database, across daylight-saving changes. Omitted: UTC. The zone used is echoed as `time_zone`. A name the host does not know is refused.

setup_instructions.title: Register the Microsoft 365 app
setup_instructions.detail: Follow docs/microsoft-365-setup.md: an Entra app registration with the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions User.Read, Mail.Read, Calendars.Read and offline_access, and MICROSOFT_365_CLIENT_ID / MICROSOFT_365_CLIENT_SECRET set on the controller. Calendars.Read is the one this module needs.

setup_instructions.title: Connect the account
setup_instructions.detail: Connect Microsoft 365 from the Talos integrations page. The controller stores tokens at 'oauth/microsoft_365/{user_id}/{account_id}/{access|refresh}_token' and refreshes them before they expire.

setup_instructions.title: Configure AUTH_HEADER
setup_instructions.detail: Set AUTH_HEADER to 'Bearer vault://oauth/microsoft_365/{your_user_id}/{your_account_id}/access_token'. For 401s, use refresh_oauth_token(vault_path) to force a refresh and inspect the outcome; a connection marked as needing reconnection must be reconnected from the integrations page.
